name: server-data
title: Server Data
description: React hooks for a PageSource on TanStack Query, behind signatures of their own: useServerPage, useServerTotal, useServerInfinite, useServerQuery, useInvalidateSource, useSourceMutation and usePageController, with DataProvider and createDataClient for the defaults.
docs: `useServerPage(source, request)` loads one page with the query key `[...source.key, "page", filter, sort, position, size]`: the previous rows stay while the next page loads (`previous`), a superseded request is aborted through its signal, and it returns `items`, `status` (`pending`, `error`, `success`), `fetching`, `total`, `navigation`, `error` and `retry`. When the source has `fetchTotal`, `useServerTotal` counts beside it, a query of its own that never holds the rows back. `useServerInfinite(source, { filter, sort, size })` adds page after page (`loadMore`, `hasMore`, `loadingMore`) by page number or cursor. `useServerQuery(key, fetch, { enabled, staleTime, placeholder, keepPrevious, select, seeds })`, from `use-server-query`, loads one resource that isn't paged (a detail, a snapshot, a short list) and returns `data`, `status`, `fetching`, `previous`, `error` and `retry`; `fetch({ signal })` is aborted when the key changes or nothing reads it, and a key under the source's (`[...tasks.key, "detail", id]`) lets the hooks below reach it. `select` picks what `data` holds (TanStack's `select`: memoised, structurally shared, typed as its result). `defineResource({ key, fetch, staleTime, seeds })` declares a resource once for every screen that reads it, through `useServerResource(resource, params, options)`; `seeds: (data) => [other.seed(params, value)]` writes other resources from an answer, mounted or not, unless the fetch was aborted or that resource got data after the fetch started. `error` is `unknown`, or the `defaultError` registered with TanStack's `Register`, or the type parameter after the data type; the page, infinite, total and mutation hooks take it too. `useInvalidateSource(source, { throwOnError })` refreshes everything under the source's key and resolves once the shown queries reloaded; with `throwOnError` (on the hook or per call) a failed reload rejects, for a toast. `useSourceMutation({ mutationFn, source, optimistic })` refreshes it once the change settles, and `optimistic: (items, variables) => items` shows the change at once and restores the rows if it fails. To write the server's answer instead of refreshing, `settleItems: (items, result, variables) => items` maps the rows of every page and infinite query under the key (totals stay) and `settle: (result, variables, current, queryKey) => data` writes every `useServerQuery` under it (`undefined` leaves one alone): they reach every cached query under the key, mounted or not, each written query's read in flight is cancelled first, nothing is requested, and the rest of the key is marked stale (a read of it already in flight starts again). A failed mutation refreshes the key unless `refreshOnError: false`. `usePageController(source, options)` keeps a `createPageController` for the component's life and follows the URL while mounted. The hooks use the app's `QueryClient` when one is provided; otherwise a shared default, so nothing has to be mounted. `DataProvider` provides one with `createDataClient` defaults when the app has none: two retries except on a 4xx (read from the error's `status`), 30 s fresh, no refetch on window focus. `createDataClient({ retry, retryDelay })` takes a number of retries (the 4xx rule stays), `false` (none) or a rule `(failures, error) => boolean`, and `isTransientError(error)` (a network TypeError, 408, 425, 429 or 5xx) writes the usual one: `retry: (failures, error) => failures < 3 && isTransientError(error)`; mutations never retry. Results reach React through TanStack's `notifyManager`, one `setTimeout(0)` after a query settles, so a test that awaits a single `act()` can see the state before it: call `notifyManager.setScheduler(queueMicrotask)` in the test setup, or wait with `findBy`/`waitFor`. With server rendering, mount a `DataProvider` per request. `useDelayedFlag(active, episode)` turns true once a load has taken 400 ms, for a status that says "Loading…" only when it matters, and `useReachEnd(onReach, enabled)` is a ref that runs `onReach` when an element scrolls into view, for infinite lists.
